builds.howItPlays: You fill the board with cheap units and 1-Might Recruit tokens from cards like Vanguard Captain and Eye of the Herald, then attack a battlefield with four or more units so Garen draws you two cards when you conquer it. When you play Spectral Matron, she brings back a unit costing 3 or less from your trash for free, so the units you lose in trades come back and your board stays wide enough to attack again.
builds.whyYou: You like going on the attack early, and you'd rather have a crowd of small units than one big threat. You enjoy the counting this deck asks for each turn: which battlefield to crowd, whether four units will still be standing after combat, which cheap unit you can afford to lose because Spectral Matron can bring it back. You don't mind that each unit is weak on its own, because together they outnumber whatever your opponent puts in front of them. If swarming a battlefield and drawing cards as a reward for it sounds fun, this Garen suits you.

builds.howItPlays: You spend your early turns on Mobilize and Catalyst of Aeons, spells that give you extra runes, and on cheap removal like Blood Money and Flurry of Blades, keeping The Ruination to kill every unit if the board gets away from you. Once you can pay 9 for Dazzling Aurora, it plays the first unit from the top of your deck for free at the end of each of your turns, often Elder Dragon, a 12-cost unit that kills an enemy unit at every location when it arrives.
builds.whyYou: You'd rather survive the early turns than race, and you like knowing that once Aurora lands, every turn puts another free big unit on the board, usually a Dragon. You don't mind playing with almost no units for several turns, holding answers and wiping the board, as long as a big payoff is waiting. Some games you won't draw your rune spells or Aurora in time, and you can live with that. If watching a free Dragon land most turns sounds better than lining up four small units for a card draw, this Garen suits you.

Deciding cards: pace from 6 to 9 rune spells (3 Mobilize, 3 Catalyst of Aeons, Blood Money Gold, Sacrifice) building to 9-cost Dazzling Aurora, 12-cost Elder Dragon and 9-cost The Ruination; stance from sweepers and removal (Flurry of Blades, Cull the Weak, The Ruination, Cataclysmic Duel, Hidden Blade, Blood Money) with only 5 to 12 units; complexity from timing ramp, holding Reaction answers and choosing when to wipe; variance from Aurora revealing until it hits a unit (steady when the only units are Dragons, swingier in yogtu2's list with more small units and Punch First) and from needing to draw ramp and Aurora on time. Legend ability: when you conquer, if you have 4+ units at that battlefield, draw 2; here it is a side bonus set up by Forge of the Future, Vanguard Armory and Corina tokens, not the main plan. Also played: none. Confidence: low.
